ambiguities.q: crown occlusion by the cyan HUD self-marker bar (x 798-805)
ambiguities.disposition: DECLARED AND BOUNDED, not resolved. On 1027 fur onset is y=416 at x806-807 and y=418 at x796-797, so the apex sits at the bar's shoulder; interpolation across the 8 occluded columns puts a hidden apex no higher than y=415. The crown could be 1-2 px higher, moving the number of record to at most 10.111 %. Both reported; the measured value stands.

ambiguities.q: lower-right dark mass on 1027 — leg or cast shadow?
ambiguities.disposition: RESOLVED TO BODY on chromaticity, discriminator stated. One-sun az 137 / el 66, so a ground shadow would be a darkened sample of floor hue. x808-816 y496-504 reads r/b 0.440/0.267 (fur); x814-820 y504-510 reads 0.350/0.316 (floor). The classifier placed the boundary at y=505; I did not choose it.

ambiguities.q: the y=422-423 gap in 1027's fur map
ambiguities.disposition: THRESHOLD ARTEFACT, declared. Those rows are the shaded skull top, r_frac dipping under 0.415; the luminance instrument shows the head continuous. Why the chroma map is a bracket and the manual read is the number.

REPORTED CONSERVATIVELY AT 817. Rows 474-477 carry fur-classified pixels to x=819 but at L 157 with r-g=74 — red telegraph arc signature, not fur (L 89-136 elsewhere). Affects w_px only; h_frac untouched.
EXCLUDED with the test shown: r/b 0.431/0.285 at L 157 — the red arc sitting exactly on the fur threshold. Admitting them would read left=756, w_px=61.

DECLARED. Three frames, three beats, 12.6 s apart at the extremes. 685 and 1027 return the identical crown row — agreement, not replication. 1062 reads 1.11 pp lower on a different standing pose. The spread is POSE spread; the camera is locked and audited.

negative_results: N1. The chromaticity discriminator holds on ONE of three frames. The carried warm omni (E 5.20, 9.0 m, colour 1.00/0.66/0.34) lights subject and floor with the same key; on 685 and 1062 the floor within that radius is itself warm and the fur test floods the lower read window. Hence the full bbox exists for 1027 alone. I did not find a second frame in 1211 where both silhouette edges are honestly adjudicable.
N2. Frame 520 passed every automated filter and failed the eye: max deviation 6 L across x 748-800, y 408-439. Dropped; sha recorded so the negative result is reproducible.

N3. Luminance-only frame selection failed twice. A wide-box darkness metric ranked the all-black end card as the cleanest frames in the clip. A red-dominance metric intended to find floating combat numerals fired at 0.197 on frame 1027 — on the werewolf's own warm-lit fur. Discarded as a HUD detector; visual triage did that job.

N4. gp_seg.py was NOT run on this clip. Its colour-distance seeding cannot separate a warm-lit subject from a warm-lit floor, which is the entire difficulty here. Skipped deliberately rather than run for the look of it.
cannot_answer: Whether the near paw sits ~9 px below the audited root row across the clip. Measured on one frame only. Applying that offset to 685 and 1062 would be desk arithmetic dressed as measurement (NOTE-62); it is offered once in the receipt as an explicit inference and nowhere else.
Whether an idle-pose register exists for this body. There is no idle frame in this clip — it is a combat watch end to end. Every number here is a standing COMBAT pose.
Whether BR2W's camera and the arena camera read the same to the eye. Out of seam. This cell supplies screen register only.
confound_DECLARED: Subject-height fraction conflates CAMERA FRAMING with BODY SIZE. The rows in this table photograph DIFFERENT BODIES. A difference in h_frac does not by itself establish that two cameras differ, and equality would not establish that they match. This cell supplies screen register for the artifact Matt ratified, and nothing else. R-CPB-17b's 'zoom/angle looks the same' is Matt's eye and gandalf's reading, not mine.
